correctness.rationale: Relational Kripke semantics under all valuations gives the exact implication (A∘B) union (B∘A) subset R; A,B reflexive make the union reflexive, and choosing any of Z missing off-diagonal pairs yields exactly 2^Z third relations. A fixed off-diagonal missing pair has probabilities (1-p)^2(1-p^2)^(2(n-2)) for the union and (1-p)^2(1-p^2)^(n-2) for one order. For any fixed finite prescribed distinct pair list, outside intermediate vertices are disjoint edge groups; within each, distinct two-edge witness events share at most one of their Bernoulli variables, giving Bonferroni 1-hp^2+O_h(p^3). The bounded endpoint set contributes 1+O_h(p). Thus uniform joint absence is (1+o(1))e^(-hnp^2), with 2h for union absence. Factorial moments yield both Poisson windows and asymptotic independence; second moments yield the concentration and c in (1,2) separation. Direct independent exhaustive n=2 and n=3 relation/valuation enumerations confirmed expansion histograms and exact one-point probabilities. Finite tests are not the proof of the limit.

originality.rationale: Aghamov-Kudinov-Nguyen-Piribauer (2026) Proposition 3.2 and Corollary 3.3 already prove the deterministic modal-frame correspondence, which is explicitly credited. Their inspected primary 15-page paper proves product modal logics and not an independent-edge random relation saturation law. Heckel-Riordan (2012) study optimized rainbow coloring of undirected random graphs, a different stochastic model from two fixed independent directed colors and the union of both ordered compositions. General random Boolean matrix products remain a priority risk; the combined double-window and third-relation count survive qualified best-of-knowledge assessment.

final_claim: For independent reflexive directed Bernoulli relations A_n,B_n and C=A∘B union B∘A, missing C pairs Z converge to Poisson(e^(-2t)) at np^2=log n+t, while X,Y each have order ne^(-t); at np^2=2log n+t, missing ordered composition pairs (X,Y) converge jointly to independent Poisson(e^(-t)). The mix modal axiom permits exactly 2^Z reflexive third-relation expansions and an intermediate regime with unique universal third relation but neither ordered composition universal.
